identity.title: ALMA observations of α Centauri. First detection of main-sequence stars at 3 mm wavelength

paper_type_evidence.quote: The binary $\alpha \, {\rm Cen\,A}$B was observed in three ALMA continuum bands, with $7.5$ GHz effective bandwidth spread over four spectral windows in each of the bands.

question.value: Can ALMA resolve the alpha Cen A and B components at mm/submm wavelengths, give their flux ratios, and extend the SED to 3 mm to probe the chromospheric temperature minimum and free-free emission?

evidence.quote: In the present context, we intend to extend the spectral mapping (SED) to longer wavelengths, where the contrast between stellar photospheric and chromospheric emission becomes increasingly evident.
This paper makes use of the following ALMA data: ADS/JAO.ALMA#2013.1.00170.S.

bands.value: Band 3 (97.5 GHz), Band 7 (343.5 GHz), Band 9 (679 GHz)

evidence.quote: The observations in Band 3, centered on 97.5 GHz (3.1 mm), were taken on 2014 July 3

continuum_bandwidth.value: 7.5 GHz effective bandwidth over four spectral windows per band

evidence.quote: with $7.5$ GHz effective bandwidth spread over four spectral windows in each of the bands.
0.2$ mJy beam$^{-1}$ (0$\stackrel {\prime \prime}{_{\bf \cdot}}$42 $\times$ 0$\stackrel {\prime \prime}{_{\bf \cdot}}$28, 47$^{\circ}$) in Band 7
the rms noise per synthesized beam in the pointing center was $0.02$ mJy beam$^{-1}$
$\sim20$ min of observing time with $\sim2$ min on-source.
were taken on 2014 July 7 using 32 antennas

provided.value: Earlier far-IR/submm photometry showing temperature minimum; 70 micron flux ratio

evidence.quote: one observation at 70 $\mu$m with *Herschel*-PACS (cite: molinari2010; wiegert2014) nearly resolved the binary
Over the wavelength range $0.09 - 70$ $\mu$m, the ratio was $S_{\!\nu}^{\rm B}/S_{\!\nu}^{\rm A}=0.44\pm0.18$
Calibration was performed using the CASA package[^2] following standard procedures
Titan was used for Band 7 (343.5 GHz, 872.8 $\mu$m)
we estimate the absolute flux calibration to be accurate to within $5\%$, $7\%$, and $15\%$ for Bands 3, 7, and 9, respectively.

self_calibration.value: Band 9 only, on alpha Cen A

evidence.quote: In Band 9, $\alpha \, {\rm Cen\,A}$ was strong enough to perform self-calibration, improving the rms noise.

weighting_robust.value: Briggs in Band 7; natural in Bands 3 and 9 (robust value not given)

evidence.quote: imaging was performed using Briggs weighting in Band 7 and natural weighting on Bands 3 and 9.
In the final, primary beam-corrected images
(cite: liseau2013)

method.value: CASA calibration with Ceres/Titan flux scales, quasar gain and bandpass calibrators; imaging with Briggs/natural weighting; B9 self-cal; primary beam correction

evidence.quote: using, for all data sets, the quasar J$1617-5848$ as complex gain calibrator

analysis_steps.goal: measure flux densities, ratios and spectral indices

method.value: Fluxes of A and B in each band; B/A ratios; spectral index alpha between bands

evidence.quote: The measured flux densities are reported in Table [\[data\]](#data) and also displayed graphically in Fig. [2](#freq).

analysis_steps.goal: compute brightness temperatures and compare with photospheres

method.value: Convert flux to T_B with stellar radius plus chromospheric height and compare to photospheric levels

evidence.quote: In Fig. [3](#alma_ab), the SEDs are presented for both stars in terms of brightness temperature[^3] versus wavelength.

assumptions.value: Chromospheric height ~0.1% of stellar radius, as in the Sun

evidence.quote: In the Sun, the height of the chromosphere $\int\!dh$ corresponds to about 0.1% of its radius.
Calibration was performed using the CASA package[^2] following standard procedures

findings_qualitative.value: First detection of main-sequence stars at 3.1 mm; both components resolved in all bands

evidence.quote: this ALMA measurement constitutes the first detection of main-sequence stars at 3.1 mm.

findings_qualitative.value: 3 mm emission greatly exceeds photospheric prediction; chromospheric free-free origin

evidence.quote: The observed 3.1 mm emission greatly exceeds what is predicted from the stellar photospheres

claims.hypothesis: ALMA can resolve A and B and give accurate flux ratios consistent with earlier estimates

evidence.quote: The new ALMA data have provided accurate flux ratios that agree with our previously estimated value.

claims.experiment: Spectral indices and comparison with photospheres
claims.result: Spectral indices 1.6-2.3, 3 mm far above photosphere

evidence.quote: The measured spectral indices are consistent with emission that is dominated by optically thick free-free processes (Bremsstrahlung).

limitations_admitted.value: Sparse spectral sampling prevents a conclusive statement on changing opacities

evidence.quote: a more conclusive statement would require a tighter spectral sampling, including the intermediate ALMA bands.

referee_caveats_inferred: Flux extraction method and errors unspecified
Band 9 calibration uncertainty is 15%, comparable to some differences
Pointing offset raises noise on B

reproducibility.rediscovery_reason: Public data, simple numeric fluxes, though details missing.
